rationale: APGAR score is the most clinically critical content in block 6 and a high-yield known-trap (not to confuse with Ballard or Silverman-Anderson)
Block 4 covers neonatal nomenclature and classification — gestational-age cut-offs are high-yield factual anchors
Block 5 covers the Golden Minute and initial stabilisation steps — the HR threshold for PPV is the most commonly tested NRP fact
Block 8 covers chest compressions and medications — the 3:1 compression-to-ventilation ratio is a classic exam point unique to neonates vs adult CPR
Block 7 covers Sarnat classification of HIE — staging is a high-yield topic and a known-trap (knowing the 3 stages and their features)
Block 9 covers management of HIE including therapeutic hypothermia — the 6-hour window is the most critical clinical fact in neonatal neurology and a known-trap
Block 4 covers the pathophysiology of RDS vs TTN vs MAS — distinguishing these three causes is the core clinical challenge and a high-yield exam topic
Block 8 covers management including surfactant therapy — the indication and timing of surfactant are must-know clinical knowledge
Block 4 covers scalp lesions — distinguishing caput succedaneum, cephalhaematoma and subgaleal haemorrhage is a classic and high-yield clinical anatomy question
Block 6 covers nerve injuries including Erb palsy — the waiter's tip posture and muscle groups affected are classic examination questions
Block 6 covers the three forms of VKDB (early, classic, late) — their timing and clinical features are a high-yield discriminator
Block 10 covers management and prevention — the IM route being superior to oral is a specific and testable policy point
Block 3 covers clinical recognition of LBW — the definition and sub-classification cut-offs are foundational facts
Block 11 covers KMC — this is a flagship low-cost intervention for LBW neonates and a frequent exam topic with specific criteria
Block 8 covers diagnosis and grading of neonatal temperature — the WHO temperature classifications are essential and testable
Block 10 covers the Warm Chain — the connection between hypothermia and hypoglycaemia is a clinical pearl that is commonly missed
Block 8 covers management of neonatal hypoglycaemia — the treatment thresholds and the 10% dextrose/2 mL/kg rule are critical known-traps (50% dextrose must never be used)
Block 3 covers neonatal glucose physiology — the definition of hypoglycaemia (<45 mg/dL) is the foundational threshold for this topic
Block 4 covers early vs late hypocalcaemia — the cow's milk / high phosphate link to late-onset is a classic clinical teaching point
Block 8 covers management — the dangerous error of rapid IV calcium is the highest-stakes clinical teaching point in this SDL
Block 4 covers aetiology and pathophysiology — HIE as the leading cause and the order of causes are high-yield facts
Block 7 covers management including the AED ladder — phenobarbitone as first-line AED in neonates is a specific and testable fact
Block 4 covers EOS vs LOS aetiology — the GBS/E. coli vs Klebsiella/Staph distinction is a high-yield knowledge point with direct antibiotic implications
Block 9 covers management — the principle of not delaying antibiotics for culture results is the highest-stakes clinical teaching point and reflects perinatal infection management
Block 3 covers timing of jaundice — jaundice in the first 24 hours being always pathological is the most tested clinical rule in neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia
Block 8 covers phototherapy and exchange transfusion — the principle that direct (conjugated) bilirubin is NEVER physiological is a critical discriminator
Block 3 covers the 5 cardinal surgical red flags — bilious vomiting being a surgical emergency is the most critical clinical teaching point in neonatal surgery
Block 6 covers clinical presentation and recognition at the bedside — knowing that failure to pass meconium by 48 hours is abnormal is a must-know fact
Block 6 covers ROP screening — the screening criteria and timing are specific, testable, and a known-trap (the screening window must not be missed)
Block 8 covers prevention and management — SpO2 targets in preterm neonates on oxygen are specific, evidence-based, and high-yield for exams
